en: The Sūtra on the Ritual Manual for the Practice of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with a Thousand Hands and a Thousand Eyes according to the Yoga of the Vajraśekhara, Volume One.
By Kai-fu Yi-tong-san-si Te-jin Shi Hong-lu-qing, Duke of Su State.

The Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Monastery—who was granted a fief of three thousand households, invested with the purple robe, posthumously honored as Minister of Works, and bestowed the title of Great Mirror of Wisdom—translates this by imperial decree, relying upon the *Yogatantra* and the *Vajraśekhara Sūtra*.
The secret practice of the Vajra Body, Speech, and Mind of the Thousand-Handed and Thousand-Eyed Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva of the Lotus Family is now explained.
The practitioner should [receive this] from a yoga ācārya.
Seeking to receive the vows of the bodhicitta discipline, one enters the great maṇḍala and receives empowerment,
thereby attaining the stage of the level of resolute belief and practice (*adhimukticaryābhūmi*).
Relinquishing body, life, and wealth,
they are courageous and diligent,
harboring a heart of compassion.
Without wearying of birth and death,
they resolutely seek to realize the body of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva and serve all Buddhas throughout successive lifetimes.
Delighting in the cultivation of the ultimate Prajñāpāramitā,
they possess loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity,
thereby benefiting sentient beings.
Whether in a superior location amidst the mountains, a secluded and pure place,
or before a clean monastery or a stūpa containing relics,
one should prepare a refined chamber and sweep and smear the ritual altar.
Banners are suspended all around, with celestial canopies placed above.
On the western side of the altar, an image of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with a Thousand Hands and Thousand Eyes is installed.
The practitioner stands on the eastern side of the altar, facing the image.
Spread mats of *mō* grass to serve as a seat,
or sit upon a small stool with feet covered by a cloth;
arrange the maṇḍala upon the altar.
Arrange the various ranks of the sages.
Place two *argha* vessels filled with fragrant water and set four precious jars at the four corners of the altar.
Every day, take various seasonal flowers and scatter them upon the altar.
Burn incense, apply fragrant unguents, offer lamps, food, drink, and various fruits;
empower these offerings and distribute them around the four sides as an act of worship.
Whenever entering the dharma hall, one should reverently perform prostrations,
confess and repent with full disclosure, rejoice in others' merit, entreat the Buddhas to turn the wheel of Dharma, dedicate the merit, and make vows; then,
one should immediately direct the mind toward visualization and contemplation.
All Tathāgatas, pervading the entirety of space,
endowed with all the primary and secondary marks, have entered the samādhi of the Dharma-realm.
Furthermore, one contemplates oneself as dwelling within the ocean-like assembly of Buddhas.
Then, one forms the seal that awakens all Tathāgatas:
with both hands, each forming a vajra-fist,
the thumbs and middle fingers hook together.
Straighten and extend the two forefingers,
with their sides touching;
recite the mantra while raising the mudrā three times.
The mantra is:
Oṃ vajratiṣṭha yojaya. While reciting this mantra and forming this mudrā, all the Tathāgatas emerge from meditative absorption.
The practitioner should reflect thus and address the Buddhas:
"My own body possesses little wisdom and little merit; I am submerged in the ocean of suffering.
I rely upon the majestic spiritual power of the Buddhas."
I only pray that you will not forsake your original vow of great compassion;
out of mercy and pity, look upon me with protective mindfulness and deliver me.
All those Tathāgatas each empower and protect him through their spiritual powers.
The practitioner of yoga attains immeasurable merit and mastery over body and mind.
Next, one should pay homage to the Tathāgatas of the four directions and request their protective empowerment.
First, one pays homage to all Tathāgatas, such as the Tathāgata Akṣobhya of the eastern quarter.
The practitioner of yoga then prostrates with his entire body upon the ground,
joining his two hands in the vajra-pañjali mudrā and extending them upward above his head.
With the mind fixed upon the ground, prostrate with utmost sincerity and reverence.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ sarvatathāgatapūjopasthānāyāntamane niryātaya me sarvatathāgatavajrasattvādhiṣṭhasva māṃ hūṃ. Having bound the *śarīra-mudrā* (body-seal), recite this mantra.
Because of making offerings, presenting gifts, and paying homage,
the yogin, by performing this prostration,
shall constantly receive the empowerment of Vajrasattva until the attainment of Buddhahood.
May the bodhicitta be brought to perfection.
Next, prostrate to all Tathāgatas, such as the Tathāgata Ratnasambhava of the southern direction.
As before, stretch out the body and prostrate fully upon the ground.
Perform the vajra-joined palms (vajra-añjali) at the heart;
touch the forehead to the ground and pay homage with utmost sincerity.
The mantra is as follows:

Oṃ sarvatathāgatapūjārcanavidhānāya niryātayāmi namaḥ | sarvatathāgatavajraratnapratiṣṭha svāhā || Having recited this mantra, one should perform the *śarīra-utsarga-mudrā* (the gesture of relinquishing the body).
By virtue of making offerings, paying homage, and showing reverence,
throughout all the stages until the attainment of Buddhahood,
one shall constantly receive empowerment from the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha, with merit perfected and endowed with all the primary and secondary marks of a Buddha.
One shall become the Dharma King of the three realms.
Next, prostrate to the Tathāgata Amitāyus of the western direction and all other Tathāgatas.
Extend the body as before.
Placing the vajra-palms upon the crown of the head,
touch the mouth to the ground and pay homage with sincere reverence.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ sarvatathāgatapūjā-pratimānayanam niryātaya me | sarvatathāgatavajradharmapratimāya svāhā. (Recite this mantra while performing the *śarīra-mudrā*.)
By virtue of making offerings, presenting gifts, and paying homage,
one shall always receive the empowerment of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara until the attainment of Buddhahood;
with wisdom perfected, one shall turn the sublime Wheel of Dharma.
Next, prostrate to all Tathāgatas, beginning with the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi of the northern direction.
Extend the body as before;
join the vajra palms and place them at the heart.
Touching the crown of one’s head to the ground, one pays homage with utmost sincerity.
The mantra is as follows:
*Oṃ sarvatathāgatapūjākarmaṇe ātmānaṃ niryātayāmi | Sarvatathāgata-vajrakarmakuru svāhā*. Then, one should perform the *śarīra-nyāsa* (placement of the body) mudrā and recite the mantra.
By virtue of making offerings, honoring, and paying respect,
one shall constantly receive the empowerment of the Bodhisattva Vajrakarma throughout all Buddha-worlds until the attainment of Buddhahood.
Having accomplished the vast activity of making offerings,
one then sits in the full lotus posture with the body upright and right mindfulness,
keeping the limbs unmoving, eyes closed, and in a state of tranquility.
One enters the contemplation of the four immeasurable minds (*catur-apramāṇa*). Then,
forming the seal of meditative concentration (*samādhi-mudrā*),
one first enters the meditative absorption of the immeasurable mind of loving-kindness (*maitry-apramāṇa-samādhi*).
With a mind of earnest purity,
one universally contemplates all sentient beings throughout the six realms and four modes of birth,
realizing that they all possess the Tathāgatagarbha.
Equipped with the three vajras of body, speech, and mind,
by the power of the merit of my cultivation of the three secrets,
may all sentient beings become equal to the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.
Having contemplated in this way, one should then recite the mantra of the Great Compassion Samādhi:
Oṃ mahā-maitrīya-sphara. Next, one should enter the wisdom of the samādhi of immeasurable compassion.
With a heart of compassion,
one universally takes as objects of focus all sentient beings within the six realms and four modes of birth,
who are submerged in the ocean of suffering of saṃsāra and fail to awaken to their own minds.
By giving rise to false discrimination, they produce various afflictions and secondary afflictions;
therefore, they fail to realize that True Suchness is equal to space and transcends merits as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
"By the power of the empowerment of my cultivation of the three secrets,
may all sentient beings become equal to the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha.
Having visualized thus, one recites the mantra of the Samādhi of Great Compassion:
Oṃ mahākāruṇya sphara; next, one should enter the samādhi-wisdom of the immeasurable mind of joy with a pure mind.
It universally takes as its object all sentient beings of the six realms and four modes of birth;
they are primordially pure like a lotus flower,
unstained by adventitious defilements, and pure by nature.
By the power of the merit of my cultivation of the three secrets,
may all sentient beings become equal to the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
Having visualized them thus, one should recite the mantra of the Samādhi of Great Joy:
Oṃ śrī-vajra-pramodana-sphara. Next, one should enter the samādhi-wisdom of the immeasurable mind of equanimity (upekṣā).
With a mind of equanimity, one universally takes as objects all sentient beings of the six realms and four modes of birth;
they are all free from "I" and "mine," free from the aggregates and elements,
and free from the grasped and the grasper, being equal with respect to all phenomena.
Because the mind is fundamentally unborn and its nature and characteristics are empty,
by the power of the merit I have cultivated through the three secrets,
may all sentient beings become equal to the Bodhisattva Gaganagañja.
Having observed thus, one should then recite the mantra of the Great Equanimity Samādhi:
Oṃ māhūcīkṣa sphara. Through this, the yogin practices the meditative concentration of the four immeasurable minds (catvāry apramāṇāni).
By reciting the mantra of the four immeasurable minds,
all various demonic activities, karmic obstacles, and difficulties pertaining to humans and devas in the future will be entirely eliminated.
Within one’s body, an immeasurable mass of merit is suddenly gathered;
the mind becomes supple and pliant, becoming capable and masterful.
Next, form the vajra-joined-palms mudrā.
With both hands, ten fingers interlaced, the right pressing over the left;
thus they are mutually entwined. The mantra is:
Oṃ vajrajāli. This is the Vajra-Interlocking-Palms Mudrā.
One will swiftly attain fulfillment of the ten pāramitās and obtain the ten masteries.
Next, bind the Vajrabandha mudrā.
Then, with the same mudrā as before, cross the ten fingers externally and form fists;
this constitutes the *vajrabandha* mudrā. The mantra is: Oṃ vajra-bandha yojaya.
The yogin swiftly attains the fulfillment of the ten stages.
Next, one binds the Vajra-bond mudrā for crushing the ten kinds of obstructions,
as previously described for the vajra-bond.
Strike the heart three times with the seal.
The mantra is: Oṃ vajramanda trāṭ. Having formed this seal, recite it.
Having been able to destroy the ten kinds of afflictive obscurations within the mind,
one then manifests and exerts the vajras of body, speech, and mind.
Next, bind the seal of the Vajra Pervasive Entry (*vajra-sarvāveśa-mudrā*).
As before, with the Vajrabandha mudrā,
bend the wisdom fingers (tarjanīs) into the palms,
each grasping the thumbs (aṅguṣṭhas).
Place it upon the heart. The mantra is:
Oṃ vajrāveśaya huṃ jaḥ. By forming this mudrā, all the three secrets of the yogin’s body become submissively compliant with the Vajra.
Maintain the empowerment without dissipation.
Next, form the Vajramuṣṭi-samaya-mudrā,
as in the previous Vajra-pervasion mudrā.
Bending the forward force to support the back of meditative concentration and wisdom, one forms the mantra:
Oṃ vajramuṣṭi vaṃ. This is the Vajra-fist Samaya-mudrā.
The vajras of body, speech, and mind are unified as one;
the practitioner of yoga will swiftly attain all accomplishments.
Next, bind the samaya-mudrā.
As before, with the vajra-bind, simply extend the *kṣānti* and *praṇidhi* fingers together to form it.
Recite the mantra three times. The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ samayas tvaṃ. One should then visualize oneself as being identical to Vajrasattva, abiding within a moon disc;
furthermore, one visualizes Vajrasattva standing before one’s body.
It is like a reflection in a mirror,
which is equal to and no different from the body itself;
this is because one has bound this mudrā and recited the mantra while remaining in meditative visualization.
One immediately attains mastery over all mudrās.
Next, one binds the Great Samaya-Truth Mudrā:
with both hands, form the vajra-bond.
The *kṣānti* and *praṇidhāna* fingers are bent to enter the palms with their tips joined.
The *dāna*, *prajñā*, *dhyāna*,
and *jñāna* fingers are held straight and upright, joined together, with the tips of the *kṣānti* and *praṇidhāna* fingers meeting.
Repeatedly touch the heart; the mantra is:
Oṃ samayam hūḥ sara tsa ta vaṃ jyūḥ. By forming this mudrā, one awakens the Vajrasattva within the body of the yogin.
By the empowerment of majestic spiritual power,
the practitioner swiftly attains the body of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
Next, bind the seal of the Victorious Bodhisattva of the Three Times.
Form the vajra-fists with both hands;
place the right hand over the left,
and hook the thumbs and wisdom fingers (tarjanīs) together in opposite directions.
Stand upright with the power of progress.
Place the seal (mudrā) at the heart.
Recite the mantra three times. The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ sunva ni-sunva hūṃ (short vowel) [same as above] | kṣiṇa-kṣiṇa hūṃ | kṣiṇa-paya hūṃ | ānaya hoḥ vāg va-jra hūṃ phaṭ. Then he entered the Vajrakrodhatejovibhūti-trilokavijaya-samādhi.
This Bodhisattva has four faces,
all of which are wrathful;
he has eight arms, each holding a weapon.
His left foot treads upon Umā;
he stands in the *tiryak-pada* (T-shaped) posture.
His entire body blazes with flames like the fires at the end of an eon.
This is the contemplation of samādhi by the supreme noble ones of the three times.
A practitioner should abide in the bodhicitta and give rise to profound compassion.
To eliminate the obstructions of those within and without, as well as gods and humans,
one should rotate the mudrā three times to the left to expel the obstructors; then,
rotating it three times to the right, one should bind the boundaries of the cardinal directions according to the desired size.
Then, seal the heart, forehead, throat, and crown of the head, reciting once for each location;
finally, release the mudrā over the crown of the head.
By binding this mudrā and reciting the mantra, [the purpose is accomplished].
Abiding in this wrathful samādhi,
all afflictions and karmic obstructions of body and mind are [cleansed] by means of the adamantine ferocity.
The fire of wisdom burns them all away.
Next, bind the Lotus Samaya Mudrā,
as before with the Vajra-bond.
Joining the *dāna* (generosity) and *prajñā* (wisdom) hands vertically, place them above the mouth and recite the mantra:
Oṃ vajrapadma samaya stvaṃ. The practitioner should then perform this visualization.
I now regard this body of mine as being identical to the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
I visualize my left hand at my heart holding a lotus flower,
while my right hand makes the gesture of opening a blossoming flower.
One abides within a perfectly full moon-maṇḍala, perceiving it with absolute clarity.
By means of binding this mudrā and reciting the mantra to empower it,
all *samādhis*, all skillful means, and the *prajñāpāramitā* [are attained].
One will swiftly attain accomplishment.
Next, bind the samādhi mudrā,
as before with the vajra-bond.
Looking upward, settle into the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*).
Extend the *vajra* fingers (*tarjanī*) and bend their middle joints, holding them upright against the back.
Cross the *dhyāna* fingers (*madhyamā*) so that they rest upon the *vajra* fingers.
Then he recited the mantra:
Oṃ samayam dhāraya hūṃ. The practitioner of yoga sits upright with his body straight, solemnly motionless.
Visualize yourself within the ocean-like assembly of all Tathāgatas.
Contemplate each Buddha-body as being as minute as a sesame seed,
yet complete with all the marks and signs, vividly and clearly manifest.
He immediately enters the contemplative wisdom of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and reflects thus:
"All phenomena are primordially pure, and I too am pure."
Because craving for the world is purified,
hatred is purified;
because the defilements of the world are purified...
Then all transgressions are purified;
because all phenomena in the world are purified,
all sentient beings are purified.
Because the perfection of wisdom is pure in the world,
omniscience (sarvajñā) is pure.
Having made this observation, the practitioner of yoga [proceeds].
Body and mind suddenly become clear and pure.
Then, one recites the mantra for penetrating the true mind (*cittapravisthāpaka*), saying:
*Oṃ jita-prati-vi-dhenga-rūmi*. The practitioner should recite this an infinite number of times.
When the two kinds of selflessness are realized,
the tathāgatagarbha is manifested,
and perfect bodhicitta is realized.
Then, recite the mantra of bodhicitta:
Oṃ bodhicittam utpādayāmi. Immediately close the eyes and clarify the mind.
Visualize within the center of your own chest a full,
pure, and brilliant white full moon;
focus your mind single-pointedly, making it difficult for the attention to shift to other objects.
Upon the perfectly luminous [sphere], one visualizes an eight-petaled lotus;
within the heart of the lotus, one contemplates the syllable *hrīḥ*,
the color of red crystal.
Then, recite the empowerment mantra of the lotus:
Oṃ tiṣṭha padma. Visualize that the lotus gradually unfolds and expands.
This continues until it completely fills the small thousand-world system, the intermediate thousand-world system, and the great thousand-world system.
Those flowers possess great radiance,
illuminating the sentient beings of the six realms and extinguishing all their suffering and affliction.
They attain peace, bliss, and joy.
Then, one recites the Lotus-Invocation Mantra:
Oṃ saṃbhara padma. One should then visualize that this lotus gradually contracts and becomes smaller.
Equalizing the measure with one's own body, one recites the *Saṃkocana-padma* mantra:
Oṃ saṃhara padma. Then, one further visualizes all the Tathāgatas in the sky.
They all entered into this lotus flower and merged into a single entity;
that lotus flower then transformed into the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
His body is the color of red beryl, and he sits upon a lotus pedestal.
On his head he wears a jeweled crown, within which a transformation Buddha is clearly and distinctly visible.
Having contemplated in this way with a resolute mind, one recites the mantra for the yoga of transforming oneself into the form of the deity:
Oṃ vajradhūḥ haṃ. By virtue of empowering [oneself] with this mantra, [one becomes the deity].
The practitioner’s own body and the body of the deity are identical and without distinction;
next, one binds the empowerment mudrā.
As before, with the vajra-bind,
join the thumbs and extend them upward, bending them like lotus petals;
when the wisdom-fingers are held side by side and extended upward, it is accomplished.
Empower the four places— the heart,
forehead, throat, and crown— with the mudrā.
Recite the mantra once for each, as follows:
Oṃ vajradharmādhiṣṭhasvāhaṃ. By binding this mudrā and performing this empowerment, the practitioner’s majestic power becomes sovereign, and they are freed from all obstacles and difficulties.
The yoga of the principal deity will swiftly attain accomplishment.
Next, form the mudrā for the consecration of the Buddha-jewel crown:
as before, perform the vajra-bind.
The kṣānti and praṇidhi fingers are held straight upward;
the vīrya and bala fingers support one another like lotus petals and are placed upon the forehead.
Recite the mantra three times. The mantra is:
Oṃ tathāgatadharmahūṃ. Having formed this mudrā and recited the mantra, [proceed].
Then one obtains the precious crown consecration of the Tathāgata Amitāyus.
Next, one forms the Lotus Garland Mudrā:
with both hands, each makes a lotus fist.
The forehead should be like a bound garland;
it encircles [the head] three times,
then divides behind the crown.
He also circumambulated three times,
slowly descending on both sides like the manner of hanging a sash.
From the perfection of generosity (*dāna-pāramitā*),
one sequentially unfolds and disperses the ten perfections.
Recite the mantra as follows:
Oṃ bhadramaṃtre dharmahṛdayaṃ svāhā. By forming the mudrā of the lotus garland, one shall become a Dharma King within the Lotus Family.
Next, bind the Vajra Armor mudrā:
form vajra fists with both hands and extend the index fingers and thumbs straight out.
Visualize the two syllables Oṃ and Tsaṃ at the tips of the two fingers, and then recite the Armor Mantra:
Oṃ vajrakavaca vajriṇi kuru vajra vajra haṃ. Recite this mantra as you follow along.
By means of the power of progression, it performs two revolutions:
first, it circles three times around the heart,
and then, having reached the back, it likewise circles there.
Returning again, it circles back to the navel;
next, it circles the right knee;
returning once more to the navel, it circles around the back.
Next, it reaches the area behind the waist,
then returns to the front of the heart,
and next circles around the right shoulder.
Next, it circles the left shoulder;
next it reaches the throat;
then it reaches the back of the neck.
It reaches the forehead first,
and subsequently the back of the head;
at each location, it circles three times.
As before, slowly lower both sides so that they resemble the shape of hanging ribbons;
from the *tārjanyāṅguṣṭha* (wisdom-finger) position, gradually extend them through the ten fingers.
Then, with both hands, rotate the fists as if dancing,
clap the palms three times against the chest,
and recite the mantra for clapping the palms:
Oṃ bhadanta tuṣye hūṃ. By binding the vajra-armour mudrā, [may it be so] until the attainment of Buddhahood, in all places and in all births.
Constantly adorned in the armor of great compassionate vajra,
may one swiftly achieve the siddhis of both the mundane and supramundane realms;
may no internal or external obstacles or vināyakas be able to harass or afflict them.
By reciting the mantra and clapping the vajra-palms,
all the noble assemblies are completely delighted.
Next, one should visualize the syllable HAṂ (with the *hu* and *gan* reversed) in the space below.
The syllable is like the color of dark indigo;
it gradually expands and widens to become a great wind-wheel.
Upon this wind-wheel, one should visualize the syllable *kṣam*.
It is white;
gradually extending and expanding, it becomes commensurate with the wind-circle and transforms into the water-circle.
Upon the water mandala, visualize the syllable *praḥ*,
golden in color;
by reciting it, the water mandala becomes a single golden tortoise.
Visualize the syllable *su* upon the back of the tortoise;
it transforms into Mount Sumeru,
composed of the four precious substances.
Furthermore, one visualizes the characters for "sword" (jian) and "flat" (ping),
which transform into a mountain of gold,
surrounded by seven tiers.
Then, in the space above Mount Sumeru,
one should visualize Vairocana Buddha,
from every pore of whose body a rain of fragrant milk flows forth.
The rain falls between the seven mountain ranges to form the ocean of fragrant water and milk endowed with eight qualities.
At the summit of Mount Sumeru,
one should visualize a great eight-petaled lotus flower.
Upon the lotus, there are eight great vajra pillars that form a jeweled pavilion;
within the pericarp of the lotus, one should visualize the syllable HṚĪḤ.
From the syllable, a great radiance flows forth,
illuminating all Buddha-worlds.
All sentient beings suffering in pain who encounter the touch of this light attain liberation.
From within this great radiance,
the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with a Thousand Hands and Thousand Eyes emerged,
endowed with immeasurable marks and signs of excellence and blazing majestic power.
The ten pāramitās surround the Bodhisattva on all sides;
the eight offering Bodhisattvas each occupy their respective positions at the four corners of the precious pavilion.
There are the *śvetā*,
the *mahāśvetā*,
and the *tārā*.
The four great bodhisattvas, such as Bhṛkuṭī and others,
were each surrounded before and behind by immeasurable hosts of the Lotus Family,
with the eight classes of devas serving as their retinue.
Visualize the infinite assembly of noble ones and the *iṣṭadevatā* in this manner with extreme clarity,
ensuring that the sequence is not lost. Then,
perform the mudrā of the Bodhisattva Dharmacakrapravartana as soon as the intention has arisen.
Form vajra-fists with both hands;
interlace the thumbs and forefingers.
Then recite the mantra as follows:
Oṃ vajracakra hūṃ jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ. Immediately place the mudrā before you upon the maṇḍala;
this constitutes the Great Maṇḍala of the World-Subduing Lotus Family.
Placing the mudrā upon the heart,
one’s own body becomes the great maṇḍala; then,
touch the image of the deity with the mudrā.
Whether that image is painted, cast in bronze, or modeled in clay,
it constitutes a great maṇḍala;
one should place the mudrā in the space before one's body.
Thereupon, the entire realm of empty space is filled to become a great maṇḍala.
Should a practitioner transgress the dharma,
erring in the three karmas and thereby breaking the samaya precepts, [the following occurs].
By binding this mudrā and reciting the mantra to empower it,
one is able to eliminate all faults and attain perfection.
Next, bind the mudrā for universally summoning and awakening all the noble assemblies.
As before, with the vajra-bind,
extend the *kṣānti* and *praṇidhi* fingers straight upward;
bend the *vīrya* and *bala* fingers like hooks, and it is thus accomplished.
The practitioner should, with a pure and elegant Brahma-voice, recite the mantra for awakening the noble assembly until it is complete.
This awakens the principal deity, the ten Pāramitā Bodhisattvas, and the holy assembly of the Lotus Family. The mantra is as follows:
āḥ jahi ghaṇṭā-ghoṣa-sugata-cīrṇa-vigatārtha-praṇamya vandate vairocana-sattva-vikrama.
1. *kāruhiṣadvaraṇa mahāmala* (with the final vowel drawn out) 2.
*ācaṇḍakasadva-viṣṭikaraka* 3. *tattvanandi* (the *ra* at the end is the same as hereafter)
Yan-ti (as above), Yan-va-ra-yam-va-ra-yam (6), A-ra-ra-kri-pa (7),
Maya Svāhā. Then, one should form the seal for the skillful summoning of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Then, modify the previous mudrā by crossing the arms at the chest with the right hand over the left; then,

One should then visualize the left hand holding a vajra-khatvanga,

The practitioner of yoga then abides in the samādhi of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
He then recited the *One Hundred and Eight Names of Praise to the Lotus Family*.

Uṣṭākeśakalabhadraṃ pañcamavāgīśvara-taraya-nitara-sahasa-rapucchaṃ saptadana-mokṣa-kṛtu.

With the two hands in the vajra-fist mudrā,

Oṃ hāya kṛvā mahāpānamaṅkuśa karṣaya svīkaraṃ sarvapadmaṅkula mañja pānamaṅkuśadhara hūṃ jaḥ. By forming this mudrā, perform the invocation.
All the assembly of noble ones has gathered.

join the two hands in the lotus-anjali gesture.
Perform the vajra-bind of the power of progress through dhyāna and prajñā.
Insert the right hand, representing prajñāpāramitā, into the mouth of the tiger held in the left hand.

All the assembly of noble ones shall be led into the great maṇḍala.
Next, form the mudrā of the Bodhisattva Padmaśṛṅkhalā:
join the two hands in the lotus-anjali gesture.
Forming vajra-fists with the thumbs and little fingers interlaced like rings,

Oṃ bhadma-sphoṭa-bandha sarva-bhadma-kūla-tamaya-cchigaraṃ hūṃ vaṃ. Having bound this mudrā, [recite as follows].
All the assembly of noble ones, by virtue of their fundamental vows of great compassion,
each remained in their respective positions within the site of enlightenment,
steadfastly abiding without dispersing.

join the two hands in the lotus-clasp gesture;

All the assembly of noble ones were greatly delighted.
Next, offer the arghya perfumed water.
Holding the arghya vessel with both hands, [proceed].

Recite the mantra seven times while visualizing that the feet of all the holy assemblies are being bathed.

Namaḥ samantabuddhānām | Oṃ gagana-samāja svāhā. When the practitioner offers the arghya water, [he should recite this].
Regarding the matter desired in one's heart,
one should immediately make a vow and address the Noble One:
"May the siddhi I seek be swiftly accomplished."
Next, form the mudrā of the Bodhisattva Padma-ānanda-lalita.
Join the two hands in the lotus-palms gesture;
extend the thumbs and middle fingers together, slightly opening them.
When this is settled in the mind, it is accomplished.
The yogin visualizes himself as identical to the Bodhisattva Hevajra;
he imagines that immeasurable Bodhisattvas Hevajra flow forth from his heart.
Make offerings to the principal deity and all the assembly of noble ones.
The mantra for the Lotus Playful Joy (*Padmanarteśvara*) is as follows:
*Oṃ padmanarteśvarāya mahānṛtyarāga-svāra-maya hūṃ svāhā*. By forming this mudrā and reciting this mantra while making offerings, [the rite is accomplished].
Before long, they will attain the stage of a Tathāgata;
dwelling in the perfection of the Dharma, they will abide in the bliss of the present dharma and realize unsurpassed enlightenment.
Next, form the mudrā of the Bodhisattva Padmamālā:
extend the arms forward from the previous mudrā and place them upon one’s own forehead and navel.
Visualize that from the forehead there flow forth immeasurable Bodhisattvas bearing garlands of lotuses,
making offerings to the Principal Deity and all the assembly of Noble Ones.
The mantra of the Lotus Garland is as follows:
Oṃ bhadramāri viśvaka pujacara kumārī hūṃ svāhā. Because one offers this mantra while forming this mudrā, [the deity is pleased].
One will obtain the perfection of the primary and secondary marks and shall become the Dharma King of the three realms.
Next, bind the Lotus Song-Praise Bodhisattva Seal.
Then, with the aforementioned mudrā, lower it to the navel;
join the hands in the lotus gesture and slowly raise them upward until they reach the mouth.
With the mudrā, pour [the offering] downward from the mouth forward.
Visualize that immeasurable lotuses and bodhisattvas singing praises flow forth from the mouth,
making offerings to the principal deity and all the assembly of noble ones.
The mantra for the Lotus Praise is:
Oṃ padmanarteśvara nāgīndra pūjaya svāhā hūṃ. By forming this mudrā and reciting the mantra, one makes offerings.
Before long, you shall be endowed with the sixty-four kinds of Brahma-voices and the four types of unimpeded eloquence,
and be able to turn the Great Wheel of Dharma throughout immeasurable worlds.
Next, form the mudrā of the Lotus-Dancing Bodhisattva.
Form the lotus-fist mudrā with both hands;
first, rotate them reciprocally at the right side of the chest as if dancing,
and next, rotate them reciprocally at the left side of the chest in a similar dancing motion.
Next, [place it] on the right cheek and then on the left cheek.
Recite the mantra continuously as before while rotating [the hands].
Finally, join the palms in the lotus gesture and place them upon the crown of the head.
Visualize that from the crown of the head, immeasurable Lotus-Dance Bodhisattvas stream forth to make offerings to the Principal Deity and all the assembly of noble ones.
The mantra for the Lotus Dance is as follows:
Oṃ bhaṭṭārikāyai sarvabuddhādhiṣṭhitāye hūṃ. Because one offers by reciting this mantra while forming this mudrā.
One shall attain three kinds of swift, mind-made bodies (*manomaya-kāya*),
and in a single instant, one shall perform miraculous displays throughout immeasurable worlds.
To bring benefit and happiness to sentient beings, perform extensive Buddha-activities.
Next, form the mudrā of the Lotus Incense-Burning Bodhisattva:
join the two hands in the lotus-clasp.
Cover both palms facing downward and scatter them.
Visualize that from this mudrā, clouds and oceans of sublime fragrance flow forth,
pervading the entire dharma realm.
To universally make offerings to the ocean-like assembly of all Tathāgatas, the mantra for burning incense with lotuses is as follows:
Oṃ padma-dhūpa-bhūja-samaye praharaṇāya padma-kurānadi mahāgaṇike padma-rati hūṃ. Because one makes this offering by binding this mudrā, [the merit is attained].
One attains the Tathāgata’s unimpeded vajra-liberation wisdom.
Next, one forms the Lotus Flower-Offering Bodhisattva mudrā:
join the two hands in the lotus-clasp.
Directing the gaze upward as if scattering flowers,
one should visualize various sublime celestial flowers flowing forth from the mudrā to universally make offerings to the ocean-like assembly of all Tathāgatas.
The mantra for the offering of lotus flowers is:
Oṃ puṣpapūjāye padmamavaśini mahāśriye padmakuḷapratīhāre sarvatathāgatasaṃdhāya hūṃ. By forming this mudrā and making this offering, [the rite is accomplished].
One attains the body of boundless enjoyment, adorned with a hundred merits.
Next, one binds the mudrā of the Bodhisattva Padmadīpa:
the two hands are joined in the lotus-anjali gesture.
The vertical alignment of meditative concentration and wisdom causes the visualization to flow forth from the seal as infinite lights of mani-jewels,
universally illuminating all buddha-fields.
The mantra for the Lotus Lamp and Candle is as follows:
Oṃ nibhābhūja-samaye padma-kurukullā-śrī-mahānuttaryā-rugjanasānaya padma-sarasvati hūṃ. By forming this mudrā and reciting the mantra, one performs the offering.

Next, one forms the mudrā of the Bodhisattva Padmagandhahasti.
With the two hands joined in the lotus-anjali mudrā,
one should separate them at the level of the chest in the manner of applying fragrant unguents.
Visualize that from within the mudrā, clouds and oceans of fragrant unguents flow forth,
making offerings universally to the ocean-like assemblies of all Tathāgatas.
Then, recite the Lotus Fragrant Unguent Mantra:
Oṃ jñānapūjācakra-samaye mahābodhisattvaguhyacarye sarvakarmāṇi me bodhisiddhi hūṃ. By forming this mudrā and reciting this mantra as an offering, [the purpose is accomplished].
One attains the fivefold Dharma-body of precepts, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation.
Next, one forms the mudrā of the Bodhisattva of the Dāna-pāramitā:
the right hand is held with the palm facing upward.
Bend the *pāramitā* of aspiration and the *pāramitā* of wisdom so that they touch each other,
while all the remaining *pāramitās* are extended.
Then recite the mantra as follows:
Oṃ bhagavati jñānabhūte viśvarūpe jana svāhā. Having bound this mudrā, recite the mantra three times.
Immediately, one extinguishes the seeds of stinginess accumulated over immeasurable kalpas and attains three kinds of merit from giving:
namely, the gift of material requisites.
The gift of fearlessness and the gift of Dharma constitute the perfection of the pāramitā of generosity (dāna-pāramitā).
In this very life, one attains abundance and prosperity.
With all necessary conditions fulfilled, one attains mastery of mind and long life.
Next, one binds the Bodhisattva Seal of the Perfection of Precepts (Śīla-pāramitā).
Interlace the two hands with the palms facing inward;
extend the thumbs and index fingers straight upward.
Then recite the mantra as follows:

Oṃ śīladharini bhagavati hūṃ haḥ. By forming this mudrā and reciting the mantra three times, the seeds of transgressions against the precepts accumulated over immeasurable kalpas are immediately extinguished.
One attains three kinds of meritorious qualities of ethical discipline:
namely, the morality of restraint, the morality of gathering virtuous dharmas, and [the morality of benefiting sentient beings].
The precept of benefiting sentient beings is the perfection of the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīla-pāramitā*).
One constantly adorns the actions of body, speech, and mind with the fragrance of ethical discipline.
All violations of the four pārājika offenses,
as well as the eight pārājika offenses committed by bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs,
are entirely purified.
In the future, one will be born according to one's vows in a pure and wondrous Buddha-field.
Next, form the Bodhisattva mudrā of the Perfection of Forbearance (kṣānti-pāramitā),
following the same procedure as the previous mudrā of the Perfection of Ethical Discipline (śīla-pāramitā).
Joining the *jñāna-bala-mudrā* like a needle,
with the *dhyāna* and *prajñā* fingers held upright,
one recites the mantra as follows:
By forming this mudrā and reciting the mantra three times— *vāgavati kṣāntidharini hūṃ phaṭ*—
one will extinguish the seeds of anger accumulated over immeasurable kalpas.
One attains the merit of the three kinds of patience (*kṣānti*):
namely, patience in enduring enmity,
and patience in accepting suffering.
Through the patient endurance of profound reflection on the Dharma,
the perfection of patience is fulfilled;
one's physical appearance becomes upright and dignified, bringing joy to all who behold it.
Without mutual hatred or envy, they all came to associate with him;
his resolute understanding was especially profound, and he could manifest transformations at will through recollection.
Next, he bound the Bodhisattva mudrā of the Perfection of Diligence (vīrya-pāramitā).
Following the previous *kṣānti-pāramitā-mudrā*, extend the fingers and separate them; this is the mantra:
Oṃ vīrya-kari hūṃ vīrya-vīrya svāhā. By forming this mudrā and reciting the mantra three times, [the rite is accomplished].
Thereby, they extinguish the seeds of karma consisting of indolence and laziness accumulated over immeasurable kalpas and attain three kinds of diligence:
namely, the diligence of donning the armor.
The diligence of gathering virtuous dharmas and the diligence of bringing benefit and happiness to sentient beings constitute the fulfillment of the perfection of diligence.
May body and mind be at peace and blissful, free from all ailments and without suffering or affliction.
May all worldly and supramundane merits, wisdom, and aspirations be fully accomplished.
Next, bind the mudrā of the Bodhisattva of the Dhyāna-pāramitā.
He then sat in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*),
with his left hand palm-upward upon his lap,
and his right hand palm-upward upon his left hand.
With the two fingers of the *dhyāna* and *prajñā* mudrās touching each other like finger-nails, recite the mantra:
Oṃ vagvati sarvapāpahāriṇi mahānāthaye hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ. Having bound this seal, recite the mantra three times.
Immediately, one extinguishes the seeds of distracted karma accumulated over immeasurable kalpas and attains the three types of meditative concentration (*dhyāna*),
namely, the meditative concentration of abiding.
The dhyāna that induces [attainment],
and the dhyāna that accomplishes tasks,
constitute the perfection of the pāramitā of dhyāna.
With body and mind rendered light and agile, the supernatural powers one cultivates will be swiftly accomplished;
no demons shall be able to invade or disturb them,
and all karmic obstructions will be entirely extinguished.
Next, bind the Bodhisattva Seal of Prajñāpāramitā:
extend the five fingers of the left hand flatly and place it facing upward beneath the heart.
Place the right hand over the left hand.
Then recite the mantra:
Oṃ śrī-sūryatā-vijaye svāhā. Having bound this mudrā, recite the mantra three times.
Immediately, one extinguishes the seeds of deluded karma accumulated over immeasurable kalpas and attains three kinds of wisdom:
namely, the non-conceptual wisdom of the emptiness of persons.
The wisdom that is empty and non-conceptual regarding phenomena,
and the wisdom that is empty and non-conceptual regarding both [subject and object],
constitute the perfection of prajñāpāramitā.
One attains brilliant wisdom and realizes both mundane and supramundane phenomena;
one becomes extensively proficient in the profound principles of the five sciences.
Next, bind the Bodhisattva Seal of the Perfection of Skillful Means (*upāya-pāramitā*):
with the right hand, hold the *prajñāpāramitā* in the position of wisdom;
with the left hand, hold the *dhyānapāramitā* in the positions of generosity (*dāna*) and ethical discipline (*śīla*).
The two hands are joined palm-to-palm with the thumbs extended straight upward like needles;
the index fingers are stretched flat and pressed against each other side-by-side.
Then, recite the mantra as follows:
Oṃ mahāmaitrīcittaye svāhā. By forming this mudrā and reciting this mantra three times, the karmic seeds of immeasurable kalpas lacking skillful means are immediately extinguished.
One attains two kinds of skillful means:
namely, skillful means regarding dedication and skillful means regarding the deliverance of sentient beings.
This is the perfection of the *upāya-pāramitā*.
By practicing the six worldly *pāramitās* and through union with this seal, mantra, and yoga, [perfection is attained].
With little exertion, their meritorious deeds become vast and manifold;
they swiftly achieve accomplishment,
all reaching the ultimate goal as provisions for unsurpassed bodhi.
Next, form the Bodhisattva mudrā of the Perfection of Vow:
extend the five fingers of the right hand straight upward,
with the palm facing outward in the gesture of granting fearlessness.
Then recite the mantra:
Oṃ karuṇi he he he saṃyukte. While forming this mudrā, recite the mantra three times.
This will immediately extinguish the seeds of karma from evil vows accumulated over immeasurable kalpas.
One attains two kinds of supreme vows:
namely, the vow to seek unsurpassed bodhi and the vow to bring benefit and happiness to sentient beings.
This constitutes the perfection of the *praṇidhāna-pāramitā*.
From the initial generation of the mind of awakening until the attainment of Buddhahood,
throughout that interval—
All sought-after supreme mundane and supramundane aspirations shall be fully accomplished.
Next, bind the mudrā of the Bodhisattva Vīryapāramitā,
following the previous procedure for the Śīlapāramitā mudrā.
The powers of dhyāna, prajñā, vīrya, kṣānti, and praṇidhāna are all held upright with their tips joined together.
Then, recite the mantra as follows:
Recite the mantra "Oṃ namo nirmuṇḍe hūṃ ha ha ha hūṃ jvala" three times while forming this mudrā.
This immediately extinguishes the seeds of inferior mental karma accumulated over immeasurable kalpas, both mundane and supramundane.
One attains two kinds of power:
namely, the power of analytical discernment and the power of cultivation.
Regarding the various remedial dharmas,
one subdues and attains the severance of all afflictions and the obstacles of delusion;
this is the resolute conviction during the stage of cultivating the path.
All celestial Māras and evil friends cannot cause them to waver;
they attain the stage of non-retrogression.
Next, bind the mudrā of the Bodhisattva Prajñāpāramitā.
Interlace the two outer hands to form fists; extend the *tarjanī* and *madhyamā* fingers straight upward, crossing them slightly at their tips.
Bend the heads of the *anāmikā* fingers so they touch each other, forming a circle.
With the hands in the *kṣānti-mudrā*, extend the fingers straight upward with the tips joined.
Then recite the mantra:
OṂ MAṆIKANYĀRI HŪṂ SVĀHĀ. Having bound this mudrā, recite the mantra three times.
Immediately, one extinguishes the seeds of innate self-grasping and innate grasping at phenomena that have coexisted for immeasurable kalpas,
and attains two kinds of wisdom of enjoyment:
namely, the wisdom of enjoying the dharma-bliss.
The wisdom that accomplishes the welfare of sentient beings eliminates the two kinds of obscurations,
namely, the afflictive obscuration and the cognitive obscuration.

The cognitive obscuration consists in realizing that all phenomena are like an illusion, like a mirage, like a dream, like a reflection, like an echo, like a shadow, like the moon in water, like a magical transformation, like Indra’s net, and like space.
Before long, one will fulfill the ten stages (daśabhūmi) and,
dwelling in the stage of the Cloud of Dharma (dharmameghā-bhūmi), become a great Dharma Master.
Next, one should form the seal of the white-robed Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
Interlace the two hands within to form fists;
extend the tips of the thumbs and touch them together so they form a circle.
With the middle fingers and wisdom fingers extended side by side, recite the mantra as follows:
Namo ratnatrayāya. Namo ’ryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya.

interlace the two hands with the palms facing inward.

Namo ratnatrayāya. Namo āryāvalokiteśvarāya. Bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya.

Before the *iṣṭadevatā*, smear a triangular mandala.
Visualize the *iṣṭadevatā* as being blue or black in color,
wearing blue-black garments.
Offer blue flowers, fragrant flowers, non-fragrant flowers,
and *māndārava* flowers and the like;
for food and drink, use pomegranate juice dyed black.
Alternatively, it may be made blue;
for the fragrant ointment, use cypress wood,
and for the arghya offering, use cow urine.
Taking small portions of black flowers, mustard seeds, deodar wood,
and unguents, place them upon the argha vessel;
then burn guggulu incense.
Then, using a lamp of mustard oil,
one should recite the mantra of Hayagrīva while maintaining a state of wrathful mind.
Alternatively, one may perform the mantra of the One-Tufted Honored One (Ekajaṭī), an emissary of the Lotus Family,
beginning from noon or midnight on the twenty-fourth day and continuing until the end of the month to complete one full cycle.
On the full moon day, perform the ritual of bathing and fasting as previously described.
By reciting the mantra in this manner, one can subdue malevolent spirits and ghosts,
as well as evil, venomous dragons that cause droughts throughout the land.
Or there may be wind, rain, frost, and hail that damage the crops; or pestilence may spread.
Furthermore, one may subdue wicked people who are disloyal to the state, as well as those who kill immeasurable sentient beings, destroy the Buddha’s teachings, and slander the True Dharma.
Icchantikas, people with false views and evil persons,
as well as various non-Buddhists who have severed their roots of goodness,
and those who harm and obstruct the transmission and upholding of the True Dharma.
Furthermore, those who turn their backs on their teachers, monks, and parents, failing to remember their kindness and virtue, and thereby creating obstacles;
as well as all malevolent beasts, insects, wolves, lions, enemies, and wicked people who wish to cause them harm.
When performing such rites as these,
those who give rise to evil thoughts will experience unease in body and mind,
as if touched by a conscious sensation.
Whether they are ill or have reached a state beyond salvation,
one should immediately exhort them to give rise to a wholesome mind;
if they can repent, reproach themselves, and forever sever their evil intentions.
He then performs the recitation for those individuals according to the rite for averting calamities (*śāntika*).
They shall thereby be freed from misfortune and suffering, seek the supreme among supramundane *siddhis*, and swiftly fulfill the two types of accumulations: merit and wisdom.
Furthermore, they fulfill the ten stages (*bhūmi*) and the perfections (*pāramitā*),
transcending the difficult practices and arduous progressions of the three incalculable eons (*asaṃkhyeya-kalpa*).
Moreover, by means of these conditions, they eliminate all internal and external obstacles.
The practitioner resolutely focuses on the single object of the samādhi of the tutelary deity.
With the three secrets in union, the mind remains uninterrupted,
relying upon the protective assistance of the great compassionate power of the vows of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
One should accomplish the requisites through the three secrets and correspond with the four seals;
the yogin should not practice harsh austerities or fixate upon specific timeframes.
It prevents the mind and spirit from becoming distracted so that one does not progress in meditative concentration;
it brings joy and bliss to body and mind throughout the four modes of conduct— walking, standing, sitting, and lying down—
and ensures that every thought-moment is in accord with the yoga of ultimate reality (*paramārtha-yoga*).
One constantly engages in contemplative practice within the pure dharma-realm;
at no time and in no place, whether by day or by night,
it is a single path of purity, just like space.
Regarding seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing, one contemplates only suchness (*tathatā*).
Regarding names and signs, one knows them all as the syllable *A*.
With objectless great compassion, self and others are equalized.
Constantly delighting in the benefit and happiness of boundless sentient beings,
may they swiftly accomplish the practices of the pāramitās and become equal to the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
If one can practice and maintain [the rite] in this manner—
whether in mountain ranges, deep valleys, sublime rock caves, or pure monasteries—
one should recite with single-minded diligence throughout the four periods of the four months.
Silently severing speech and exerting body and mind,
one does not indulge in sleep or indolence; rather,
one accords with the practitioner’s faculties— whether sharp or dull— and their distinctions in pure faith and resolute conviction.
In the interim, one will certainly attain pliancy (*praśrabdhi*), and the samādhi will manifest before them.
Within that very concentration, they will see countless Buddha assemblies,
hear the sublime sound of the Dharma, and realize the stages of the ten grounds (*daśabhūmi*) and the various pāramitās.
Having perfected the transformation of the basis (*āśraya-parāvṛtti*) of body and mind,
one realizes unsurpassed enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*) after sixteen great lifetimes.
For those who seek supramundane accomplishment:
Having already entered the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu and received the initiation of the Vidyādhara of the Principal Deity,
one has fully received from the Ācārya the mudrās, mantras, yogas, and contemplative practices.
Draw the image of the principal deity according to the ritual manual,
in accordance with one's capacity and personal preference.
This should be done in an auspicious and blessed location, together with companions and disciples who are knowledgeable in the Dharma.
Furthermore, having accomplished the necessary provisions and conditions,
the disciple must be reverent and filial toward the teacher, skillfully complying with their wishes,
possessing pure faith in the profound Dharma, and abiding in the bodhicitta.
Regarding the capable companions:
for the sake of accomplishing a single type of *siddhi* together with an unshakable mind, there are four categories of objects sought for accomplishment.
The first consists of the wheel, hook, sword, vajra, and battle-axe.
First, items such as staffs and mendicant’s walking sticks;
second, substances such as yellow orpiment, cinnabar, ox-gall, and various medicinal herbs;
third, taking earth from both banks of a river to fashion the forms of various birds and beasts.
These refer to elephants, horses, water buffaloes, chickens, geese, peacocks, garuḍas, and so forth.
Fourth is the image of the tutelary deity (iṣṭadevatā),
which is accomplished according to the teachings of the Susiddhikara-sūtra.
Furthermore, one should fashion the maṇḍala of accomplishment and so forth,
as well as medicinal substances, images of birds and beasts, and representations of the deity— including their specific dimensions,
proportions, and physical characteristics— as well as white woolen cloth woven by a maiden.
Depending on which of these [methods] one falls upon, perform the accomplishment.
Having completed the full number of preliminary mantra recitations, then,
together with companions and disciples who know the Dharma, [proceed].
With time limited by days, months, and years,
one should exert great diligence day and night,
like a person drilling for fire who must not allow an interruption.
One seeks the manifestation of the three signs,
namely warmth, smoke, and light.
When the practitioner is about to attain proximate accomplishment, [these signs appear].
When various obstacles arise,
one should perform homa rites for subjugation, pacification, and so forth,
according to the superior, middling, or inferior materials for accomplishment.
Some grasp [the vessel], some smear it on their bodies, some ride upon it, or hold it in their hands;
they fly through the air together with their companions and spiritual friends.
Some people see the accomplished practitioner (siddha) in this manner.
Alternatively, those who achieve accomplishment shall see that person fly up and travel through all worlds,
making offerings to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
All shall have a lifespan of one great kalpa and attain the hundred dharma-gates of illumination of the first bhūmi.
If one relies solely upon this method of recitation, [the result will be as described].
Whether once, twice, thrice, or four times a day,
one should perform the mudrās and recitation before a sacred image in a pure room,
maintaining the practice constantly without interruption.
In this very life, one will certainly attain purity of the three karmas;
all sought-after worldly splendor and nobility will be fully accomplished,
and one will obtain abundant wealth and treasures.
He is one whom all people joyfully wish to behold;
he is profoundly learned in the sūtras and śāstras, his fame resounds throughout the ten directions,
and he is protected and sustained by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Sleeping in peace and awakening in peace, one cannot be harmed by any demons.
At the time of death, the tutelary deity will appear before them,
and they shall proceed to the womb of a lotus flower in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
